title: Why Do We Mourn Departed Friends
description: Why Do We Mourn Departed Friends in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER OLD, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 574 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Comfort under Bereavements”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER OLD; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Why do we mourn de-part-ed friends, Or shake at death's a-larms? 'Tis but the voice that Je-sus sends To call them to his arms.

lines: Why do we mourn departed friends,
'Tis but the voice that Jesus sends
To call them to his arms.
Why should we tremble to convey
There the dear flesh of Jesus lay,
The graves of all his saints he blest,
Where should the dying members rest,

licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to WINCHESTER OLD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
